document:
Exercise: Single Leg Butt Kick

Category:
plyometrics

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- plyometric

Primary Muscles:

- quadriceps

Secondary Muscles:

- calves
- hamstrings

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2

Energy Requirement:
high

Recovery Time:
1.5 hours

Goals:

- enhance_quadriceps_strength
- improve_explosive_power

Contraindications:

- condition: knee injury, description: This exercise may exacerbate knee injuries due to the high impact nature of the movement.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single Leg Tuck Jumps, instructions: ['Begin by standing on one leg, with the bent knee raised.', 'Using a countermovement jump, take off upward by extending the hip, knee, and ankle of the grounded leg.', 'Immediately flex the knee and attempt to touch your butt with the heel of your jumping leg while tucking the legs together.', 'Return the leg to a partially bent position underneath the hips and land. Your opposite leg should stay in relatively the same position throughout the drill.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Single Leg Jumping Jacks, equipment: body only

Instructions:

- Begin by standing on one leg, with the bent knee raised. This will be your start position.
- Using a countermovement jump, take off upward by extending the hip, knee, and ankle of the grounded leg.
- Immediately flex the knee and attempt to touch your butt with the heel of your jumping leg.
- Return the leg to a partially bent position underneath the hips and land. Your opposite leg should stay in relatively the same position throughout the drill.
